editorial.evidence: 16 November 2026: read all 46 captured sections (about 19,000 words) of the workflow-orchestration source and wrote the casebook from scratch. The brief opens on the six-system process and the irreversible payment, defines workflow, activity, side effect, business-level exactly once, idempotency key, compensation, saga and durable history before use, and adds an o-123 example taken from the source's own code and tests. Tutorial parts 1-4, 6 and 7 became walkthrough steps 1-8; part 5's records, code and tests, the retry formula, the four trade-offs and the coverage-notes gap essays moved to deep dives, with source section numbers replaced by links. Bullet-list source material was rewritten as connected prose, and list-shaped data (question tree, must/should/could, scorecard, phases, risk register, 50-minute plan) became tables. All three code blocks and all 14 figure pairs are kept beside their explanations; of the ten source tables, seven are reproduced, the two blank worksheet templates became prompts with authored worked answers, and the old sections table became reading guidance. Additions are labelled: an illustrative backoff schedule, the o-123 traces, two authored worksheet answers, an implementation trace, and caveats that the test fixtures are undefined and the no-double-charge sketch does not prove durability. Repeated sentences (the history/receipt rule, retry-storm partitioning, the outcome line) were consolidated where they repeat. No source item was omitted. November 21 complete maintained-baseline review: All five sections of reliable-workflow-orchestration: brief, eight walkthrough steps with all figures and tables, records, saga code, tests, retry, trade-offs, gap sections, references, every practice reveal and the Quick review. Targeted corrections and source-to-output mappings: /Users/sourav/Github_Repos/Forward-Deployed-Engineer-Interview-Prep/.website_spec/casebook-review-24-33-2026-11-21/reliable-workflow-orchestration/audit.json. Historical captured-source mappings remain preserved; this pass audits the maintained baseline. Source inconsistencies settled in text (2026-11-21): Saga code refunds on a permanent email failure while the failure-policy table lets email degrade → the walkthrough now says only order-voiding failures trigger the refund and a refund after a CRM write needs a CRM compensation, because the policy table is the design and the code is a narrow sketch.; Stripe reference said a late retry falls back on the stored ActivityReceipt, but the crash drill is defined by that receipt being missing → the note now adds a provider lookup by business reference for that case, because otherwise the hardest crash has no recovery path..
